classification_counts.reconciliation: urban_dominant + mixed + rural_dominant + unclassified = colorado_zctas (500); the 23 unclassified are exactly the DHC-unmatched ZCTAs, mostly small/rural codes also flagged in the ranking coverage audit.

limitation: ZCTA-level comparison of urban-dominant vs rural-dominant areas by Census-2020 urban population share -- NOT point-in-polygon classification of each charger. Mixed ZCTAs are reported as their own class. Full geospatial classification is the later H3 stage.

vintages.households_denominator: 2024 ACS 5-year B25003 (from the frozen modeling table)
vintages.vintage_caveat: These sources span different years and collection methods. The urban/rural split is from the 2020 Census point-in-time, while households, income, and renter cost burden are 2020-2024 ACS estimates, and EV/station data are 2026 snapshots. Comparisons are descriptive; a ZCTA's urban share could have shifted since 2020.

urban_dominant.density_method: AGGREGATE: sum(ports over the class) / sum(households over the class) * 1000, so large and small ZCTAs are weighted by their household counts (NOT an unweighted mean of per-ZCTA ratios).

mixed.density_method: AGGREGATE: sum(ports over the class) / sum(households over the class) * 1000, so large and small ZCTAs are weighted by their household counts (NOT an unweighted mean of per-ZCTA ratios).

rural_dominant.density_method: AGGREGATE: sum(ports over the class) / sum(households over the class) * 1000, so large and small ZCTAs are weighted by their household counts (NOT an unweighted mean of per-ZCTA ratios).

interpretation_notes.dcfc_corridor_hypothesis: Higher DC-fast density toward rural ZCTAs is a POSSIBLE interpretation (highway-corridor fast charging rather than neighborhood Level 2), NOT a verified geographic finding: this analysis does not locate chargers relative to highways or confirm corridor placement. It would need station coordinates and road data (the H3 stage) to verify.
interpretation_notes.zero_supply_sensitivity: The rural zero-supply share softens with a minimum-household floor (see share_zero_supply_by_household_floor): the DIRECTION of the finding is robust (rural ZCTAs are far more likely to lack public charging at every floor), but the MAGNITUDE of the headline 64% is partly driven by very small rural ZCTAs (rural median ~442 households). Report it as a coverage gap, not a precise rate.

renter_cost_burden.definition: share of renter households paying >=30% of income on gross rent (ACS B25070 buckets 007-010), excluding the "not computed" category (011) from the denominator
renter_cost_burden.coverage: All statistics are computed ONLY over the Colorado ZCTAs with valid B25070 data (n_zctas below; 437 of 500); the 63 unmatched or zero-rent-computed ZCTAs are excluded. These are NOT all-Colorado figures.
renter_cost_burden.statistic_labels: median_across_zctas = unweighted median of per-ZCTA shares (a typical covered ZCTA); household_weighted_estimate = sum(burdened renters)/sum(rent-computed renters) over the covered ZCTAs (a typical renter household in a covered ZCTA, ~53%, NOT a statewide all-renter rate). The "51%" headline is the median_across_zctas.
renter_cost_burden.moe_note: ACS 5-year estimates carry margins of error that are proportionally larger for small renter populations; per-ZCTA shares for tiny areas are noisy and should be read as indicative, not precise.
